videos.script:
Today the planner becomes a planner. {{data}} Three courses, six sessions, and a week you can move forwards and backwards.

You build it with four runes. A rune is a word the compiler recognises, written with a dollar sign.

The first is state. {{state}} State is a value the page depends on. You change it with an ordinary assignment, and the page follows.

The second is derived. {{derived}} A derived value is computed from other values, like the week's total. You never set it. It keeps itself right.

Then deep state. {{deep}} An array of sessions you can push onto, and an object whose fields you can assign. Svelte sees each change, and only the parts of the page that read it update.

The third is effect. {{effect}} An effect reaches outside the component, like the title in the browser tab. You will also learn the rule that matters more: when not to use one.

And the fourth is props. {{props}} Props are how one component hands values to another. The week's total becomes a small component of its own, used twice.

By the end, the page has three values you set by hand, and everything else on it follows from them.
